Q: PlacePictureInCell API for Office.js A:

I'm afraid that Office.js does not have anything equivalent to the VBA function that you mentioned. Perhaps one of the following will work in your scenario:

Use Range.getBoundingRect() (in preview) or calculate row heights and column widths to position the image at the cell’s top‑left corner.

Set the picture’s height and width to the cell’s dimensions.

Office.js supports picture.placement, but this still does not replicate “Place in Cell” behavior fully. These workarounds mimic the effect but do not reproduce Excel’s native anchoring.

Q: C++ struct default initializer declarations, what is best? A:

std::vector is default-constructible, so there is no need to explicitly specify an initializer for it at all. And as such, MyConfig is also default-constructible and doesn't need to be initialized explicitly.

Q: Count number of digits in a number A: 
function getlength(number) {
    return number.toString().length;
}

UPDATE: As discussed in the comments, the above example won't work for float numbers. To make it working we can either get rid of a period with String(number).replace('.', '').length, or count the digits with regular expression: String(number).match(/\d/g).length.

In terms of speed potentially the fastest way to get number of digits in the given number is to do it mathematically. For positive integers there is a wonderful algorithm with log10:

var length = Math.log(number) * Math.LOG10E + 1 | 0;  // for positive integers

For all types of integers (including negatives) there is a brilliant optimised solution from @Mwr247, but be careful with using Math.log10, as it is not supported by many legacy browsers. So replacing Math.log10(x) with Math.log(x) * Math.LOG10E will solve the compatibility problem.

Creating fast mathematical solutions for decimal numbers won't be easy due to well known behaviour of floating point math, so cast-to-string approach will be more easy and fool proof. As mentioned by @streetlogics fast casting can be done with simple number to string concatenation, leading the replace solution to be transformed to:

var length = (number + '').replace('.', '').length;  // for floats

Q: What is the difference between React Native and React? A:

React Native is a cross-platform using React for building apps with the same code for all platforms like (iOS, Android, Web, Windows, Mac, and Linux).

The difference in implementation is React using HTML tags, but React Native is using React Native-specific components.

Q: Math for incrementing a counter for a very large progress bar where total doesn't fit in an int A:

So the value should change past every multiple of T/100 where / is the exact division

Let T=100*q + r

The ith change of bar is when P >= i*q + (i*r)/100

You precompute 100 values i*q+ceil( i*r/100 ), that is i*q+(i*r+99)//100 where // is integer (either truncated or floor) division.

The last part can be performed with small integer arithmetic (since r<100)

All in all, you have to precompute 100 large integer multiplications.

Then a large integer increment and a large integer comparison per loop.

Q: Alerting on a failed cron job A:

To get an email every time a cron job, you have scheduled to run, fails:

  1. Redirect all of your standard output to /dev/null or to some file.

  2. Use the MAILTO environment variable with a list (comma separated) of all the email addresses you want to receive the email notifications.

To avoid using the same value of MAILTO for every task you run, you can just write it in the crontab e.g.:

MAILTO="foo@bar.com"
0 5 * * * /bin/some_script > /dev/null

MAILTO="foo@bar.com" to the top of a crontab will cause any output from the cron job to be emailed. So we redirect the STDOUT to null and if any STDERR messages are present, they will get emailed to you.
